News.title: Tiger Woods seen describing to cops his car crash before he is arrested on suspicion of DUI charges
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Newly-released body cam footage captured Tiger Woods during his arrest for a DUI following a car crash on Jupiter Island last Friday.

The footage shows the golfer down on one knee with his arms crossed and appeared to be cooperative with deputies as he told them what happened.

“I looked down at my phone and all of a sudden – boom,” he told deputies on the scene.

Woods, 50, was driving on Jupiter Island on Friday when his Land Rover clipped a machinery truck and flipped over.

In the video, Woods is checked out by a sheriff’s deputy who tells him they will have a medic will check him out.

He was assessed by Drug Recognition Experts on the scene and after it was determined that he was “impaired”, with his eyes “bloodshot and glassy”, and he was taken to the county jail for testing.

Tiger Woods was captured on bodycam video during his arrest after a car crash last Friday ( Law&Crime )

According Sheriff Budensiek, Woods tried to go around the pickup truck pulling a trailer when he hit the trailer, lost control and flipped his SUV.

It happened on South Beach Road shortly before 2pm.

The driver of the pickup truck tried to edge off the side of the road to avoid a collision but with this being a small two-lane street, there was “no shoulder” for the vehicle to move into.

In the body cam footage, the Land Rover can be seen on its side as deputies speak to the driver of the pickup.

Neither Woods, who was the only one in his Land Rover, nor the driver of the pressure washer vehicle were injured in the crash.

“He was not injured,” Sheriff Budensiek said a press conference earlier this week. “Again, he was lethargic on scene, but that we believe was because of what he was intoxicated on.”

Woods pleaded not guilty for driving under the influence. He was released on bail.

“I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today,” Woods said in his first public comments since the crash. “I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritize my well-being and work toward lasting recovery.

“I'm committed to taking the time needed to return in a healthier, stronger, and more focused place, both personally and professionally. I appreciate your understanding and support, and ask for privacy for my family, loved ones and myself at this time.”

His next court appearance was scheduled for May 5, though he does not need to appear in person.

Shoaib Bashir revealed he has spent much of his first few weeks at Derbyshire in the nets as he looks to give himself every chance of reclaiming his spot as England’s first-choice spinner this summer.

Despite being England’s only frontline spinner in Australia, Bashir was overlooked during last winter’s 4-1 defeat, with all-rounder Will Jacks offering the point of difference to the pacemen in four Tests.

While Bashir is pragmatic about the snub, he is leaving no stone unturned with his new county, having moved to the Central Co-op County Ground on a two-year deal after rejecting a new Somerset contract.

open image in gallery Shoaib Bashir was relegated to substitute fielder and drinks carrier during the Ashes (Robbie Stephenson/PA) ( PA )

“I’m always looking to learn,” the 22-year-old said. “I’m still so young and I don’t take that for granted at all. I keep working hard. It’s nice to live close to the ground so I can pop in whenever.

“I’m doing extra all the time; batting, bowling indoors. Even if I can get a net outdoors, I’ll come on my own and just bowl in the net because I’m so eager to develop and learn.

“I’ve got a massive ambition to play for England. It’s the most special thing and the most honourable thing that you can do, so I’ll do anything in my powers to try and improve.”

Derbyshire head coach Mickey Arthur, who has overseen Australia, South Africa, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, waxed lyrical about his new arrival, at one point exuberantly describing him as a “national treasure”.

While pointing out there will be ups and downs for Bashir, Arthur, whose side begin their Rothesay County Championship campaign on Friday against Worcestershire, believes he has a gem on his hands.

open image in gallery Will Jacks, right, was England’s spinner in four Ashes Tests (Robbie Stephenson/PA) ( PA )

“I’ve been very fortunate to see a lot of spinners, some in the subcontinent, I haven’t seen a spinner that is as consistent as what Shoaib is at the same age,” Arthur said.

“The growth is going to be massive and what we do is give them the roots to grow and the wings to fly. From what I’ve seen with Shoaib, the world is going to be his oyster.”

Bashir was plucked from obscurity by England two years ago and claimed 68 wickets in 19 Tests, backed by the management despite inconsistent displays and Jack Leach being preferred to him at Somerset.

His 6ft 4in frame and overspin on bouncy Australian pitches meant he had long been earmarked for the Ashes to try to replicate Nathan Lyon, who himself had a peripheral role before succumbing to injury.

open image in gallery Shoaib Bashir did not play an Ashes Test over the winter ( PA Wire )

England captain Ben Stokes insisted during the series Bashir, the youngest England men’s bowler to take a five-wicket haul, remains his number one spinner, with Jacks preferred to bolster the batting.

“Obviously it was very situational and the team was selected on a game-to-game basis and spin didn’t play a massive part in the Ashes,” Bashir said.

“I’m in communication with the England management a lot and I definitely feel that they’re keeping an eye on me and seeing how I’m improving and tracking the things that I’m learning.”

After warming the bench and carrying drinks in Australia, Bashir, whose last England appearance was nine months ago after breaking a finger on his non-bowling hand against India, flew out to Zimbabwe for a specialist camp with former Pakistan spinner Mushtaq Ahmed.

“I just wanted to get some time to spend with him and, honestly, I learned a lot,” Bashir said of the link-up with Mushtaq, who was part of England’s coaching staff at the Under-19 World Cup in Zimbabwe.

open image in gallery Shoaib Bashir has turned to former Sussex and Pakistan spinner Mushtaq Ahmed for help ( Getty Images )

“I only spent a week with him and I learned a lot about my action, really small technical tweaks that have helped me in pre-season. I’m looking forward to working on those because I feel like they will make a massive difference.”

PA

News.title: How much does it cost to run an air fryer? This is what the experts say
News.content:
Speak to anyone who owns an air fryer and you’re bound to hear all about how convenient and cost-effective they are. But if you’re considering buying one yourself, you may be wondering whether those claims really stack up. That’s why we’ve consulted experts from AO, Uswitch and Salter to find out how much an air fryer really costs to run.

Energy has become a huge topic of conversation again with the war in Iran pushing up prices. For now, most of us are protected by the energy price cap, which is set to drop in April to £1,641 until the end of June. But in July, experts from the energy consultancy Cornwall Insights predict that our bills will increase by around £300 a year.

If you haven’t already, it’s worth experimenting with new ways to cut costs, particularly in the kitchen. For me, this has involved passive cooking – when you turn off your stove before the food is cooked and the residual heat finishes the job – as well as adding a slow cooker and, yes, an air fryer to my kitchen.

As you would expect, the cost of running an air fryer depends on what model you buy and how exactly you use it. I consulted the experts to get their advice on both – here’s what they said.



How much does it cost to run an air fryer?

It’s no coincidence that the popularity of air fryers has soared at the same time that the price of energy has increased.

“The cost to run an air fryer can vary based on factors such as wattage and price of electricity, but on average, if you use a 1,500W air fryer for 30 minutes, it costs around 18p to 21p per use,” says Isabella Forgione, small appliances expert for AO.

This tracks according to my calculations. The best budget air fryer, the Judge 4l, would cost around 20p to use for 30 minutes based on recent energy prices.

What affects the cost of running an air fryer?

The exact cost of running your appliance depends on a few factors, including whether you have a single or dual air fryer.

“Dual air-fryers tend to cost more to run than single air fryers if both compartments are in use at a given time, due to more energy required to power them,” says Forgione. “They also tend to be higher voltage than single air fryers, which again can cost more to run.”

This is something to bear in mind when you’re shopping for an air fryer, says Ben Gallizzi, energy expert at Uswitch. “Make sure you choose the right model for your household’s needs. It is not very efficient if you have a two-drawer model but only use one drawer most of the time.”

Saul Davis, buying director for Salter, also recommends considering energy efficiency before you buy your air fryer.

“Several factors influence how much it costs to run an air fryer, including its size and power rating, how long you cook for, and the temperature you select,” he explains. “Your household electricity tariff also makes a difference, as energy prices vary between suppliers.”

Is an air fryer cheaper to run than a conventional oven?

Each of the experts I spoke to agreed that cooking with an air fryer is cheaper than using an oven on average. “Air fryer use has gone up enormously in recent years, partly because they are so energy efficient compared with ovens,” says Gallizzi.

As well as using less energy per minute, air fryers also tend to cook food more quickly than an oven, Gallizzi explains. “One advantage of air fryers is that they get to the right temperature quickly and food often does not need to be cooked for as long as it does in an oven. Cooking a jacket potato, for example, might take around 30 minutes in an air fryer, but 60 minutes in the oven.”

However, there is a caveat. “Bear in mind that using an oven can be more cost-effective than an air fryer if you are cooking lots of elements for a meal, such as a roast dinner, or if you are batch cooking,” says Gallizzi. Although, home appliance tester Rachael Penn has written a guide to how to cook an entire Sunday roast in an air fryer.

The best air fryers to buy

Ninja 15-in-1 foodi max air fryer Ninja’s 15-in-1 foodi max came out on top in our review of the best air fryers. Not only does it have a vast array of functions, such as pressure cook, sauté and even yogurt, it’s also easy to use, according to tester Rachael Penn. “It even sounds an alert halfway through cooking, so you know when to give the basket a little shake,” she said. She also found it “straightforward to clean”, as you can simply “remove the inserts and pop them in the dishwasher”. £319 from John Lewis Prices may vary

Judge 4l air fryer Dubbed the best budget air fryer in Rachael Penn’s review, the Judge 4l is currently less than £40 at Wayfair. It’s a no-frills appliance, operating with just two dials, and Rachael highly recommends it for couples and small families. “It cooks really well – my chips came out crispy, and the device did a good job of evenly cooking chicken,” she said. £46 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary

Tips for saving money

There are lots of ways that you can be energy-conscious when cooking with an air fryer so that you can cut costs even further. “Try to cook full portions where you can. Preheating is often unnecessary, so skipping it can save energy,” says Davis.

“Making sure food is spaced out properly helps air circulate, allowing it to cook more evenly and quickly. Keeping your air fryer clean also helps it run efficiently.”

Forgione also had some nifty tricks. “Cutting your food into smaller chunks before putting it in your air fryer can significantly reduce your cooking time and therefore the electricity needed to do so.”

She also advised against trying to cram too much food in the air fryer at once. “Overfilling your air fryer drawer can often cause internal blockages, which can lead to more energy required to power your air fryer efficiently,” she says.

News.title: Iran’s Pasteur medical research centre ‘heavily damaged’ in strike
News.content:
A century-old medical research centre set up to fight infectious diseases like plague and smallpox has been heavily damaged in strikes on Tehran, Iran’s health ministry has said.

The Pasteur Institute of Iran, which is one of the country’s leading public health centres and is part of a global research network, plays a key role in combating infectious diseases like cholera and Covid-19.

Hossein Kermanpour, a spokesperson for Iran’s health ministry, condemned the attack as a “a direct assault on international health security,” calling the centre “a century-old pillar of global health”.

He called on the World Health Organization (WHO), the International Red Cross and global health institutions to condemn the attack and assess the damage and support its reconstruction.

Photographs from the site showed severe damage, with large parts of the facility reduced to rubble.

A series of loud explosions struck Tehran on Thursday, shaking buildings and sending shockwaves across the city, according to local media reports. Blasts were felt in central, eastern and western areas of the capital.

Esmail Baghaei, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson, called the attack on the facility “heartbreaking, cruel, despicable and utterly outrageous”.

“This is not merely another war crime committed as part of an illegal war; it is a barbaric assault on basic human core values,” he wrote on X.

The Telegraph has approached the US military’s CENTCOM and the Israeli military for comment.

News.title: A TV critic’s guide to the best streaming services (and the ones worth reconsidering)
News.content:
A quick quiz question. What were the first original hits for streaming giants Netflix and Amazon? On Netflix, it was the Kevin Spacey-starring political drama House of Cards in 2013. On Amazon, it was police procedural Bosch, which premiered the following year.

That’s a measure of how far on-demand TV has come in such a short time. It took our traditional terrestrial broadcasters half a century to reach critical mass and become production powerhouses. The streamers have managed it in little more than a decade.

Never before has so much ­small screen entertainment been so easily available. But in a crowded and confusing market, how do you find the right streaming service, or services, for you? To help you decide, we’ve provided a guide to all the platforms available in the UK, comparing their cost, content and more, so you can confidently decide which is worth your money. Let the streaming wars begin…

The best TV streaming services: At a glance

Best Buy TV streaming service: Netflix

Amazon Prime Video Best TV streaming service for families: Disney+

Disney+ Best TV streaming service for quality over quantity: Apple TV

Apple TV Best TV streaming service for sports: Now

Note: All prices listed below are the starting costs and were accurate at the time of publication.

How to choose the best TV streaming service

Naturally, the most important factor for choosing a TV streaming service is the quality of the content. There’s an element of subjectivity here, depending on your personal tastes and the age ranges you’re catering to, but the big hitters tend to have a broader range of programming to appeal to more viewers.

If one show is especially important to you, it’s worth doing your research before subscribing. Visit the Just Watch website, type in the show you want to watch, and you’ll see a summary of where it can be streamed.

Beyond that, price is also important. While streaming platforms tend to be competitive, subscribing to multiple providers can quickly see costs spiral. Typically, subscription costs range from £3.99 per month all the way up to £34.99 per month if you care about live sports, but cheaper tiers sometimes compromise on image quality and other features, or may be ad-supported.

Finally, consider how easy each platform is to actually watch. Big players like Amazon, Netflix and Disney+ don’t just have smartphone apps, but easy-to-use software for smart TVs and games consoles. Smaller rivals may force you to use a web browser for a bumpier experience.

News.title: Alistair Brownlee: ‘I’ve been in a swimming pool zero times since retiring’
News.content:
How old were you when you started to compete professionally? Mary-Grace, East of England

I did my first triathlon when I was eight, but didn’t compete professionally until I was 18.

I won the World Junior Championships, and I did some serious races the year after I was 19. I went to the Beijing Olympics as a 20-year-old the year after.

What advice do you wish you would have received when you considered a career in sports? Ekaterina, London

My parents, my dad in particular, recommended that I studied alongside sport when I was young.

I also had some brilliant advice from my coach Malcolm, who told me to believe that I could win the Olympic games – but only by one stride, which was a great way of saying have faith but not too much, and train really hard.

Endurance sport, although it sounds a bit cliché, is a long game. Don’t rush things, look after your body, focus on the small things: nutrition, sleep, recovery, all of that, and that will pay dividends over a long period of time.

What was it like competing so hard against your brother and could you put the result to one side after the race was over? Caroline, East of England

I didn’t know any different. I’ve competed against my brother since I was really young – six-years-old or probably even younger in the garden at home so it’s very natural to me.

Even at the top level of the sport I think we took it for granted. We would be training side by side at home in Yorkshire one day and competing in the top races in the world the day after.

We basically knew that we were each other’s best training asset and we also knew that we could help each other in racing as well as the training.

We pretty much always put it aside straight after the race, and that was partly about our relationship and partly because we both had that kind of mentality, we were always thinking about the next thing.

Who was your biggest competitor and why? Nicolle, South East

Obviously my brother Jonny was a big competitor throughout the main part of my career.

I also had a very talented, ferocious Spanish competitor called Javier Gómez. I raced him probably 100 times during the same period. He came second at the London Olympics and beat me to the world title quite a few times.

We were very close in physical ability, and well matched in terms of where we were in the race. Quite a few of our races came down to sprint finishes.

The new facilities at the stadium will include a brand new pitch, safe standing and a fan village.

Plans include ripping up the current surface and digging down several feet to install what the club believe will be the best pitch in the division next season.

New high-tech floodlights are also on the way, capable of syncing with music to create a modern matchday experience while cutting energy costs.

The overhaul doesn’t stop there, with upgraded LED advertising boards set to replace the current system, which reportedly racks up huge monthly running costs.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Gunners face set-piece nightmare in FA Cup as Invincibles star’s son, 13, in squad for massive tournament
Sports.content:
ARSENAL risk having their set-piece plans scuppered when they head to Southampton on Saturday.

The Gunners are travelling to Saints in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup – and the Championship club could have a few tricks up their sleeves.





Oxford United boss Matt Bloomfield fumed when his side visited St. Mary’s last month as the advertising boards were moved.

It prevented Oxford from making the most of their long throw-ins from Myles Peart-Harris and Ciaron Brown.

Bloomfield argued it endangered players’ safety and a tape measure was eventually brought out to ensure the boards were the correct distance from the side of the pitch.

Arsenal risk having the same done to them given their notorious threat from set-pieces.

And Mikel Arteta’s side have already experienced advertising boards being moved this season, when they went to Sunderland in November.

The Black Cats did so to stop Arsenal’s long throw-ins and went on to claim a 2-2 draw at the Stadium of Light.

HIT THE JAK-POT

ARSENAL will bank an extra €2million (£1.7m) if Porto sell Jakub Kiwior this summer.

The defender, 26, is currently on loan at the Portuguese club and they can make the deal permanent at the end of this season for €15m (£14.8m).



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Porto are expected to do so as Kiwior has performed well this term to help them climb to the summit of the Portuguese top-flight.

There have been suggestions that Porto may then look to immediately sell the Polish international in search of a quick profit.

Juventus are among the clubs interested in the centre-back, who would likely command more than £14.8m in the current market.

But if Porto do look to make a swift sale then Arsenal can at least take some comfort from a further cash windfall.

As part of the loan deal that took Kiwior to Porto, the Gunners are due a fixed amount of €2m (£1.7m) from any future sale.



REISS LIGHTNING

REISS NELSON is working hard to get himself fit ahead of a big end to the season.

The Arsenal winger has had a tough loan spell with Brentford this term, where he has failed to break into the team.

Injuries have not helped and Nelson spent the first part of last month on the sidelines with a calf issue.

He got 45 minutes under his belt this week, though, for Brentford’s Under-21 side in their 6-1 win over Fleetwood Town’s U21s.



Nelson scored and set up another goal before coming off at half-time as part of a pre-planned sub.

The winger will hope it is the start of a strong end to the season as he faces a crucial summer back at Arsenal.

Nelson is into the final year of his contract at the Emirates and there have been no talks over a new deal.

MU KID ON THE BLOCK

RISING star Luis Munoz continues to impress for Arsenal at youth level.



The 14-year-old wonderkid scored a brilliant solo goal and registered two assists as Arsenal’s academy took on Charlton.

Munoz picked up the ball in his own half, beat four players and fired a drilled effort into the bottom corner for his goal.

The teenager has been tipped for big things at Arsenal and has already trained with the first team this season.

In addition to his involvement with the senior squad, Munoz made his U18s debut last month, scoring a 90th minute equaliser off the bench to earn the young guns a 2-2 draw with Fulham.

This all comes in the same season that Munoz became the youngest player ever to play in the Uefa Youth League.



The talented youngster was just 13 years and 11 months old when he took part in the Arsenal U19s’ 4-2 win over Bayern Munich in November.

FATHER LIKE SON

THE son of former Arsenal ace Jeremie Aliadiere has been named in the provisional Arsenal U15s squad for the Next Gen Beijing Cup in China.

Leo Aliadiere, 13, is following in his father’s footsteps as he tries to make the grade in North London.

The versatile teen can play as an attacking midfielder, winger and striker and has already attracted sponsorships.



Last year, Leo penned a deal to become an Adidas athlete.

Dad Jeremie also joined Arsenal as a youngster, going on to make 50 first team appearances and being a part of the Gunners’ Invincibles squad.

Sports.title: Dark history of DR Congo’s last World Cup under different name, from pay row to being ‘threatened’ by president’s guards
Sports.content:
THE Democratic Republic of Congo are heading to the World Cup for the first time in 52 YEARS this summer.

But the last time they went to the tournament, their country had an entirely different name.





Former Manchester United stars Axel Tuanzebe and Aaron Wan Bissaka were two of the pivotal stars that helped lead the African nation back to the World Cup, with the former scoring the winning goal against Jamaica in the play-off to secure their place.

Back in 1974, Zaire would become the first Sub-Saharan African country ever at the World Cup Finals – the very same year the country held Muhammed Ali vs George Foreman in Rumble in the Jungle.

Although Egypt was the first African country in a World Cup back in 1934, it wasn’t until 1974 a black African country made their bow.

It’s believed that’s mostly due to years of rejected applications and qualification rules put in place by Fifa that seemingly made things far more challenging for the Sub-Saharan teams



From just after gaining independence from Belgium in 1960 to 1971, the country was known as Congo. Dictator Mobutu Sese Seko – we’ll call him Dictator Mobutu – renamed it Zaire, but once he was overthrown in 1997, the country re-emerged as the Democratic Republic of Congo.

While all laws and power sources were being centralised by the new Zaire government led by Dictator Mobutu, the country had progressed through a gruelling qualifying phase that saw just one African side earn a place at the World Cup in West Germany.

They beat much-fancied Morocco 3-0 in a decisive final group stage match and went on to win the African Cup of Nations that followed at the start of 1974.

Despite the turmoil at home, underpinned by the First Congo War that started in 1966, Zaire had become a formidable force in the world of football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They didn’t have Premier League stars like Tuanzebe and Wan-Bissaka in their ranks in those days. Although there was a few singular cases, the mass migration of African stars to top European sides didn’t start in earnest until the 1980s and 90s.

But they did have the ‘Black Beckenbauer’ Tshimen Bwanga. They also had AFCON ’74 top scorer Ndaye Mulamba, who was the captain of the team at the finals.

These days, fans have been spoilt with the rich talents that have come out of the African continent, whether it be Roger Milla and his seductive hips at Italia ’90, Jay-Jay Okocha running amok at USA ’94 or even Senegal shocking France to kick off the 2002 iteration of the event.

Mohamed Salah is one of the most famous footballers on earth. Yaya Toure is one of the all-time great Premier League midfielders, as is Didier Drogba when it comes to strikers. The lists go on and on.

But the world was far smaller in 1974. This was before social media, scouring networks and, well, the internet!



So Zaire arrived in West Germany as an unknown quantity, but touted as potential surprise packages.

They had the task of taking on the formidable Brazilian team of the 1970s, a Scotland team with Kenny Dalglish and Dennis Law among others and a dangerous Yugoslavia outfit, but they were not short on belief.

They opened up against the Scots, who struggled to deal with the energy and pure attacking intent.

Scotland may have underestimated them, but they managed to escape with a 2-0 win which many argue was against the run of play.



Zaire, led by their Yugoslavian coach Blagoje Vidinic, would then face his home country in their next outing. What unfolded next left a stain on African football for a myriad of reasons, but perhaps what transpired was misunderstood in real time.

Dictator Mobutu was understandably elated when the team qualified for the tournament. Excited to project his vision of Congo’s African strength, the dictator allegedly bought all of the players new houses and cars.

He also set up a deep cash kitty for the players to dip into during the tournament if they needed it and an enormous entourage of government and Zairian football officials to accompany the team.

However, after just the first game, it was quickly realised the kitty was nearly gone thanks in large part to all of the sticky fingered officials who had flown over.



The players soon discovered this and not only learned that their World Cup fund was nearly bled dry, but that cash reserve was supposed to be their wages and bonuses for the tournament, too.

Furious with the betrayal from their own people, a large part of the Zaire squad decided they would not play against Yugoslavia and go on strike. This caused Fifa to intervene and pay the players 3,000 deutsche marks themselves, if only to save the tournament from embarrassment.

What followed was a Zaire team bereft of pride or desire reluctantly taking to the pitch. They would lose 9-0 to Yugoslavia, tied-first for the heaviest defeat in World Cup finals history.

Did they throw the game after backstabbing turmoil in their own camp? Did they fail to prepare and, bereft of enthusiasm, suffer the consequences? Or were they simply handed a lesson on the pitch?



It’s hard to say. But what the eyes could see was a sloppy display. Either poor players or players who looked poor. It was an embarrassing look for Zaire and African football, lending credence to those who looked down on them to begin with.

Scotland manager Willie Ormond had said: “If we can’t beat Zaire then we should pack our bags and go home.” That’s what the footballing world thought.

But would it have been worse if the world knew the real struggles going on behind the scenes? That might have been even worse for their image.

So the world was kept in the dark at first and there was one more encounter to deal with before their World Cup was over – facing the champions Brazil.



Zaire had become the joke of the World Cup by this point. Already eliminated and on the end of a history-making beating; the idea of facing one of the best Brazil sides was the worst possible tonic.

You won’t be surprised to learn that someone like Dictator Mobutu was not thrilled with being humiliated. He decided to get involved again.

Fullback Mwepu Ilunga has since claimed in an interview given to the BBC that the Brazil game quite literally became life and death.

He said: “After the match, he sent his presidential guards to threaten us. They closed the hotel to all journalists and said that if we lost 0-4 to Brazil, none of us would be able to return home.”

Why 4-0 is the magic scoreline for Dictator Mobutu, we don’t know.



Then comes the moment that has made every World Cup highlights package ever since.

Brazil held a 2-0 lead over the tournament first-timers in the final Group B match. Just 10 minutes remained when the legendary duo of Rivelino and Jairzinho stood over a free-kick.

But, before they could take it, Zaire defender Mwepu Ilunga broke from the wall, sprinted at the Brazilians and hoofed the ball up field.

Ilunga was surely unaware he was about to attain football immortality and to the naked eye, it looked like somebody who didn’t truly understand the rules of the sport he was playing.



BBC commentator John Motson even called it “a bizarre moment of African ignorance.”

But it wasn’t ignorance. It wasn’t stupidity, either. It was fear. It was a time-wasting tactic designed to confuse Brazil as the Zaire team knew they could not afford to lose 4-0.

Brazil did end up scoring again, but the game finished 3-0 and the Zaire team was safe to return home – but not welcomed.

From national heroes to shamed, penniless, outcasts; almost every career of the players was instantly over.

Mobutu swiftly changed his tune on football. He cut funding to the national team and the sport became almost frowned upon in the country for a generation.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Now, Congo rises from the ashes of the suppressed Zaire to take its place in the newly expanded 48-team World Cup. They will be one of 10 African teams at the finals and they have many players operating in the top leagues around Europe.

Congo is now a nation reconnected and they’re ready to re-write their nation’s story.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Fede Valverde was urged to have surgery for rare throat problem that made him sound like Mickey Mouse
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID star Fede Valverde was forced to undergo throat surgery after a rare condition left him with a high-pitched voice likened to Mickey Mouse.

The midfield powerhouse revealed he struggled for years with the issue, with doctors repeatedly telling him he needed an operation but his family simply couldn’t afford it at the time.





Valverde said during an interview on Terapia Picante: “When I spoke, I had a problem in my throat and I was always advised to have surgery.

“We were a humble family and couldn’t pay for an operation overnight.

“We thought it was just something from adolescence, that it would change, but it never did.”

The problem became the subject of online jokes after a clip of him aged 17 at Club Atletico Penarol went viral, with fans mocking his squeaky voice and comparing him to Mickey Mouse.



Thankfully, the issue has now been resolved, with Valverde admitting: “Now it has changed, thank God – but at the time I suffered.”

Despite the setback, the Uruguay ace has gone on to become one of the biggest stars in world football, even captaining both club and country in 2026.

But his journey to the top was anything but smooth.

Valverde also opened up on feeling completely out of place after arriving in Madrid as a youngster, admitting he was “crushed” by the culture shock.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “I thought, ‘I don’t know what I’m doing here.’ My teammates had amazing cars and designer clothes- I didn’t want to even take mine off in the dressing room.”

On the pitch, though, it was a different story.

Known for his thunderous shooting, Valverde even revealed he once injured Luca Zidane, son of Zinedine Zidane, leaving him fearing the worst.

He admitted: “I was devastated. I thought they were going to fire me.”

He recently scored a hat-trick against Manchester City that helped Madrid progress to the quarter final of the Champions League.



His impact at Madrid has left many again hailing the club’s scouting system having brought him in early just as they did with Vini Jnr and Rodrygo.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss makes rarely-seen move in furious post-match interview after being sent off in Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
FUMING Chelsea boss Sonia Bompastor was so angry at a bad refereeing decision she got out her phone during the post-match interview to prove how clear the incident was.

Bompaster held up her phone to the BBC cameras as evidence of what she thought should have been a red card for opponents Arsenal.





The decision wasn’t given and Chelsea were knocked out of the Champions League quarter-finals by their London rivals.

Arsenal looked set to have Katie McCabe sent off when the full-back pulled the hair of Alyssa Thompson during a Chelsea attack in added time.

Despite VAR being in play, the Gunners escaped punishment – leaving Blues boss Bompastor seething.



So angry was the Chelsea boss that she herself was sent off by the referee.

In her post-match chat on the BBC, Bompastor pulled up game footage of the Ireland captain grabbing Thompson’s hair.

Bompastor said: “I brought the phone with me, I don’t know if you can see that.

“But if you look at this video, for me it’s clearly the red card for the Arsenal player. She’s pulling Alyssa’s hair.



“I just think it’s not good enough.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“At the end I’m the one who gets a red card where I think the Arsenal player should be the one who gets a red card.

“What is the VAR doing in these games? If we have the VAR, why are we not checking these situations?

“I don’t understand, and it’s not good enough.”

The French manager initially saw yellow for her touchline protests, but was soon sent down the tunnel.



Bompastor added: “At the end, I’m the one who gets a red card, where I think the Arsenal player should be the one who gets a red card.”

Chelsea were trailing 3-1 after the first leg.

The second leg ended 1-0 to Chelsea after Sjoeke Nusken scored the only goal of the game in the 94th minute.

If it wasn’t for McCabe’s hair pull, the Blues would have had one last opportunity to find an equaliser.

But the hosts didn’t get that chance and ultimately lost 2-3 on aggregate and were eliminated from the Champions League.



McCabe wrote on socials: “I just want to clarify that I was genuinely reaching for the shirt, I wouldn’t ever want to pull someone’s hair.

“Full respect to Thompson.”

In the first leg of the quarter-final, Stina Blackstenius, Chloe Kelly, and Alessia Russo put three past the Blues at the Emirates.

Lauren James recovered one for Chelsea as the tie ended 3-1.

Holders Arsenal will now progress to play either Lyon or Wolfsburg in the first leg of the Champions League semi-final on April 25.



They face each other tonight in France, but Wolfsburg lead after a 1-0 win in the first leg.

Sports.title: I tried out VR technology Odegaard is using to get back to his best for Arsenal – his brain is so fast it left me dizzy
Sports.content:
MARTIN ODEGAARD has missed over 120 days of action this season through injury, but fortunately for Arsenal, he is using cutting edge tech to keep sharp for his return.

The Gunners captain, 27, leans into the world of Virtual Reality to keep his brain match-sharp without any physical burden during his rehab.





Odegaard, who is fighting to return from a knee injury in time for Arsenal’s FA Cup quarter-final with Southampton on Saturday, is one of a host of modern-day pros focusing on training their ‘scanning’ to improve their game.

Scanning – how a player takes in information on the pitch – has become one of the most useful skills in football, with so many of the top players lauded for how they can paint a picture of the game around them before they even receive the ball.

And it’s a big reason why Odegaard is still fourth for chances created per 90 minutes in the Premier League this term, behind only Bruno Fernandes, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

The Norwegian is the king of reading the game and knowing exactly where his team-mates – and opponents – are at any given moment.

Part of that is down to his use of Be Your Best, a handy piece of VR tech that simulates in-game situations and trains players in scanning using AI and cognitive science.

Odegaard was the first of a wave of pros to adopt the software, which was developed after research showed the best players in the world are those who can scan the most.

Now, over 10,000 players, including Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Guehi and Romeo Lavia, use it to better their game.

In its simplest terms, scanning is the process of taking small glances away from the ball to check your surroundings, but for the elite players it means they are always one step ahead of their opponents.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Be Your Best CEO Andreas Olsen thinks that edge can be the difference between being a great player and a world-class player.

Olsen told SunSport: “We believe that we will play an important part in the journey of a player, and we can be an accelerator to improve your cognitive skills. That’s what we are striving for.

“When it comes to the pro players, like Tchouameni, before he started to use it, he was already at a good level.



“But for him, improving by just one per cent can actually mean the difference between becoming a really world-class central midfielder for Real Madrid and being a good central midfielder for Real Madrid.”

Tchouameni first started using VR ahead of a game he played at centre-back for Real Madrid, wearing the headset to get used to playing in the backline and the situations he would face from those positions on the pitch.

For Odegaard, the tech is about making his return to the pitch feel easy.

The team at Be Your Best had to introduce their own ‘Odegaard Mode’ that simulates a Premier League level game at 120 per cent speed, after the Arsenal ace maxed out the previous settings with ease.

Odegaard wanted something that would make his return to action feel slow in comparison to the rehab work he had been doing.



SunSport got their hands on the industry-leading tech and even got the chance to try out ‘Odegaard mode’, with the fast-paced scenarios leaving us dizzy and unable to realise we even had the virtual ball at our feet at times.

The tech, which 80 different clubs have adopted, registers how often players scan and whether they can carry out what is called a ‘critical scan’.

A critical scan is defined as a final glance away from the ball while a pass is already on its way to a player.



Odegaard is brilliant at this, and was even seen advising Arsenal academy kids to take ‘one last look over your shoulder’ when receiving the ball in a clip from his recent documentary.

Over the course of a game, Odegaard scans almost 500 TIMES on average, meaning he is constantly taking in information about what is around him.

In the 10 seconds leading up to the ball arriving at his feet he looks away roughly seven or eight times, far more than the three to four times an average Premier League player glances away.

It’s why the midfielder so often looks like he has far more time on the ball than he actually does.

Mikel Arteta will be hoping that Odegaard’s extracurricular activities will help him slot straight back into action ahead of a crucial run-in for the Gunners.



With Ebere Eze ruled out for several weeks due to a calf injury, Odegaard’s creativity could be the key to Arsenal finally getting over the line in their quest to end a 22-year wait for a league title.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Despite six different injuries hampering his ability to play consistently this season, Odegaard still ranks first for assists per 90 and second for passes into the final third per 90 at Arsenal this season.

And with his VR training only helping him stay sharp, Arsenal fans will be hoping he will rediscover that form as soon as he gets back out on the pitch.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola 'delays' final decision on staying at Man City with new deadline set
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola 'delays' final decision on staying at Man City with new deadline set

Manchester City won't find out what Pep Guardiola's next move will be until the season finishes, with the Catalan delaying any decision until the football is over

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola has a contract until 2027, but could leave this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola won't make any decision on his Manchester City future until the end of the season, with the Catalan still considering calling it a day at the Etihad.

‌



The former Barcelona boss has a contract until the end of next season, but noise continues over whether he may opt to leave his post 12 months early. If that is the case, then those in charge on the blue half of Manchester won't find out until the season is done.

‌



The Telegraph report that Guardiola wants to analyse in May where City are under him, how he feels, and then decide on whether or not to do another 12 months in his role. But as things stand, the 55-year-old has genuinely not made up his mind regarding his future.

‌



City have undergone a rebuild at the Etihad following their historic four-in-a-row run of titles. It has resulted in the likes of Marc Guehi, Antoine Semenyo and Rayan Cherki all moving to the club as Guardiola seeks to regenerate his squad.

The team remain in the Premier League title race, but do trail Arsenal by nine points with a game in hand. They are in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup and have already claimed the Carabao Cup, which they achieved by beating rivals Arsenal at Wembley.

Premier League confirm TV picks as Man Utd get rare slot and Man City handed title boost READ MORE :

The FA Cup final is on May 16 and the Premier League season finishes on May 24. There remains the possibility of City completing a domestic treble, but they will need several things to go their way. It remains to be seen whether that incentivises Guardiola to remain or not.

‌



The uncertainty means that City's hierarchy are having to consider what they do should Guardiola move on. They've had to compile a shortlist of possible replacements, which features former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, ex-Real Madrid head coach Xabi Alonso and former player Vincent Kompany, who's in charge at Bayern Munich.

View 2 Images Man City won't find out about Pep Guardiola's next move until the season ends (Image: Getty Images)

Hugo Viana, City’s relatively new director of football, would be the man spearheading a search for a new manager but is also leading the club’s transfer strategy. Several of the club's targets would likely want reassurances over who their head coach would be before signing. City also have some of their stalwarts running out of contract, among them captain Bernardo Silva.

Article continues below

Guardiola is the longest-serving manager in the Premier League by some distance. The current City regime have rarely had to change the man in the dugout. Across their near two decade ownership they've only hired three managers - Roberto Mancini, Manuel Pellegrini and Guardiola.

Sports.title: Real Madrid unhappy with England after Jude Bellingham's 'pointless' trip
Sports.content:
Real Madrid unhappy with England after Jude Bellingham's 'pointless' trip

Jude Bellingham failed to play a minute for England during the recent international break - leaving Real Madrid angry given that their star had only just recovered from an injury

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham was part of this month's England camp

Real Madrid have been left frustrated by England's handling of Jude Bellingham after they called him into camp - only to leave him on the bench for both games during the international break.

‌



The Three Lions convened for friendlies at Wembley, first with Uruguay and then with Japan. They drew with the South American nation before a shock loss to Japan on Tuesday.

‌



Thomas Tuchel named an expanded 35-man squad for the two games, allowing him to look at more players, but Bellingham was among the major names included. Bellingham has been returning to full fitness following a hamstring injury he picked up in early February and only made a brief cameo off the bench in Real's victory over Atletico Madrid two weeks ago.

‌



Nevertheless he flew back to his homeland to be part of England camp, but failed to play a single minute. Marca report that Real feel that their player returning to England only to sit on the bench and be part of training was 'a pointless trip'.

Los Blancos are in the midst of a La Liga title race, where they trail Barcelona by four points. They're also gearing up for a heavyweight Champions League clash against Bayern Munich, and they want Bellingham firing on all cylinders.

Man Utd bosses fear new transfer issue thanks to Andre Onana contract clause READ MORE :

Arsenal urged to beat Chelsea in summer transfer race for ex-Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Tuchel admitted that playing Bellingham presented "too much of a risk" as he explained his decision to overlook the midfielder, who has by no means been a guaranteed starter in his England side. He told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think it's too much of a risk. So, the tendency is that he [Bellingham] will not play.

‌



"We have all gained from him being part of it. He was excellent in training, but he was involved as a neutral player. He was involved in not the whole 100 per cent of the training. So, it looked very, very good but we're still holding him back, to not take a risk.

View 2 Images The midfielder has only just returned from an injury layoff

"The injury is a muscle, it's a very particular one, and we absolutely don't want the re-injury in this moment of the season. And him as well, it was very good that he was in camp. He was excellent. But the tendency is that he won't play."

Article continues below

Madrid believe that Tuchel's decision to snub Bellingham has "done little to help" the midfielder ahead of their upcoming games. Meanwhile, Bellingham's club team-mate. Trent Alexander-Arnold, was afforded some extra rest after being a surprise omission from Tuchel's squad - with there being a genuine possibility he could miss out on the World Cup.

Sports.title: Man Utd bosses fear new transfer issue thanks to Andre Onana contract clause
Sports.content:
Man Utd bosses fear new transfer issue thanks to Andre Onana contract clause

Andre Onana could land himself a hefty Manchester United pay rise despite being absent all season with a likely return to the Champions League seeing the squad benefit financially

View 2 Images Man Utd were happy to let Andre Onana leave in the summer, but face an imminent decision on his future (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United's charge towards the Champions League could see Andre Onana land a pay rise despite being absent all year - and it could make it all the more challenging to offload him in the summer.

‌



The Red Devils have been without the Cameroon goalkeeper for almost the entire season following his shock loan departure to Turkish side Trabzonspor. There was no obligation or option to make the move permanent, meaning he is set to return to Old Trafford in July.

‌



Onana was signed by Erik ten Hag in 2023 but he was part of a squad-wide pay cut that occurred after United failed to reach Europe for the 2025-26 campaign. It meant the players got hit with a 25 per cent reduction, so as to offset the lack of European revenue.

‌



But United sit third in the table and a return to the Champions League would see the players' salaries return to their original levels. The Sun reports that figures at United are concerned that the increase in salary will make it more challenging to get Onana off their books.

Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged READ MORE :

Man Utd told Elliot Anderson would fancy Newcastle return over Old Trafford switch READ MORE :

The player himself though, who previously played in a Champions League final with Inter Milan, is determined to stay and fight for his place in Manchester.

United signed Senne Lammens from Royal Antwerp for £18million in the summer when he was relatively unknown, but he's since established himself as their No 1. The Belgian has impressed and now commands the jersey.

‌



A return for Onana could leave United having to carry a very expensive goalkeeper as their back-up. Should they want to send him out on loan again they may have to pay a portion of his salary just to get him off their books. They currently have the luxury of Trabzonspor paying his entire salary.

View 2 Images Andre Onana is currently on loan at Trabzonspor (Image: Gerrit van Keulen/Getty Images)

United's willingness to move Onana on for the year came after two error-strewn years, which eventually saw him dropped for a brief period by former boss Ruben Amorim. After replacing David de Gea, despite his ability to play out, it quickly became evident that he was not as good a shot stopper.

Article continues below

Amorim said on his exit: “Sometimes it’s hard to point where things went wrong. The performance, the moment, the bad luck in some moments was hard on him. I wish the best for Andre. He was really hard working and good at helping the players. But sometimes you need to change the environment.”

Sports.title: Casemiro shows up Ruben Amorim with striking comment on Man Utd team-mate
Sports.content:
Casemiro shows up Ruben Amorim with striking comment on Man Utd team-mate

Kobbie Mainoo is a key part of Michael Carrick's Manchester United side after struggling for game time under former manager Ruben Amorim.

View 2 Images Casemiro has made his feelings on Man United teammate Kobbie Mainoo clear (Image: Manchester United/YouTube)

Casemiro has appeared to disagree with former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim on Kobbie Mainoo, naming his teammate as ‘one of the best’ in his position. The Brazilian's comments flew in the face of what Amorim had said about Mainoo previously, insisting he could be the world's best for the next 12 years.

‌



Mainoo found himself on the sidelines under Amorim and was unsure of his future at the club, even contemplating a loan or permanent exit amid interest from Chelsea and Napoli. He has, however, been reintegrated into the starting lineup by interim manager Michael Carrick and has been flourishing for the club again.

‌



The academy graduate has started every game under the stewardship of Carrick, which earned him a place back in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the current international break. Mainoo featured in both friendlies against Uruguay and Japan and will be bidding to earn a place on the plane for this year’s World Cup.

‌



Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged READ MORE :

Premier League clubs ranked as Man Utd left in the dust by rivals cashing in on academies READ MORE :

Under Amorim, Mainoo failed to start a Premier League game this season, with his only start coming in the shock Carabao Cup defeat against Grimsby Town. It led to Mainoo pushing to leave the club in the summer window.

But the 20-year-old's immediate impact since coming back to the fold post Amorim has shown up the club's former boss. Several big-name pundits and club icons were baffled at his lack of game time and now Casemiro has twisted the knife by tipping him to go on to stardom.

“Kobbie is the present and the future,” the Brazilian said in a Q&A with United. “I think that he is one of the best No.8s and can be for that for the next 12 years.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“He is a player I really like. He always wants the ball. It is true that football can’t change your mentality but Kobbie demonstrated that he hasn’t changed his focus once.

“He has to continue focusing like he is now and continue playing the important role he is now. But what a player he is, he is a great player.

‌



"He has demonstrated this, in the Euros final with England, he has demonstrated it in finals, he scored in the FA Cup [Final, vs Man City in 2024]. Kobbie is the present and the future.”

When questioned back in December why Mainoo wasn’t getting game time, Amorim bit back. "You always ask me the same thing,” he said.

"I understand what you are saying. You love Kobbie. He starts for England, but that doesn't mean I need to put Kobbie on when I feel I shouldn't."

‌



View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo has been an ever-present in Michael Carrick's starting line-up for Manchester United. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Steven Gerrard is among the pundits to have recently blasted Amorim’s treatment of the player . “I felt really sorry for him in terms of the kid’s career under Amorim,” he told TNT Sport.

“I think it was out of order that he never got any opportunity, especially with Man United being so inconsistent.

Article continues below

“But not surprised that Michael Carrick [started to play him]. I think that was one of the straight wins if you walk into a job, if you like. Get Kobbie Mainoo back in, get him smiling, give him game time and minutes, and get him fit and up to the speed where we all know he can play.

“He’s now at a level where he walks in the England squad, never mind Amorim not playing him. He walks into the England squad if he’s playing regularly for Man United.”

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to beat Chelsea in summer transfer race for ex-Real Madrid star
Sports.content:
Arsenal urged to beat Chelsea in summer transfer race for ex-Real Madrid star

Como ace Nico Paz, who was once of Real Madrid, has shone for the Italian side and Arsenal have been encouraged to pursue the Argentine despite interest from the likes of Chelsea

View 2 Images Nico Paz has excelled in an impressive Como outfit

Arsenal have been urged to land Como's Nico Paz this summer despite former club Real Madrid having a buy-back option and Chelsea also being keen.

‌



The Gunners have continued to invest heavily in their squad and, more recently, spent big to land the likes of Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze. They have helped spearhead their pursuit of the Premier League this term.

‌



Now Owen Hargreaves thinks they should go after Paz, who has been a shining light in a Como side that have exceed expectations in Serie A. They sit in the Champions League spots with the Argentine midfielder scoring 11 times in all competitions.

‌



Paz, who is managed by former Arsenal star Cesc Fabregas, has been at the Italian side since 2024 when he left Los Blancos. The Spanish giants are believed to have the option to re-sign Paz but Hargreaves thinks Arsenal need to move for the 21-year-old, who could see his stock rise at the World Cup this summer.

The former England star said on TNT Sports: "There’s a young lad at Como, Nico Paz. There’s an option for him to go back to Real Madrid but if I’m Arsenal… This kid – you’ll see him at the World Cup. Mikel Arteta will already know that this boy will be a star and if you don’t ask you don’t get. A player like that could suit Arsenal."

Viktor Gyokeres sends key Arsenal message Mikel Arteta will love ahead of title run-in READ MORE :

Premier League confirm TV picks as Man Utd get rare slot and Man City handed title boost READ MORE :

Fabregas has seen Paz's quality up close and he looks like a bargain having joined for just €6million (£5.2m). Back in November he said: "Nico does incredible things. He is a footballer capable of pulling a trick out of his hat at any moment." Last week he doubled down on that view as he said: "He sees the goal, he is not afraid. Nico enjoys playing, he can play different roles and he is very complete player. I see a very, very big potential in him."

‌



Arsenal may have to make several decisions regarding their frontline this summer. Ethan Nwaneri has had to head out on loan with Mikel Arteta struggling to give all of his players their desired game time.

View 2 Images The Argentine was previously at Real Madrid, who could look to bring him back

Gabriel Martinelli, Bukayo Saka, Leandro Trossard, Eze and Madueke are among the wide options available to him with Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus vying for the No 9 shirt. Kai Havertz remains a versatile option.

Article continues below

Despite that wealth of attacking talent Arsenal have been criticised for an over reliance on set pieces. The Gunners have set records for the amount of goals they've scored from dead ball situations, leading to suggestions they lack a cutting edge in open play.

Sports.title: FIFA world rankings confirmed ahead of World Cup with new No.1 after England lose
Sports.content:
FIFA world rankings confirmed ahead of World Cup with new No.1 after England lose

The field for World Cup 2026 is now complete with the international break over and there is a new World No. 1 topping the FIFA rankings

View 3 Images England were beaten 1-0 by Japan to end the latest international break (Image: Getty)

England remain fourth in the FIFA world rankings after a lacklustre international break. But it's all change in the World No. 1 spot with Spain supplanted.

‌



The Three Lions entered this break with friendly games against Uruguay and Japan on their doorstep. Their opening fixture at Wembley ended in a disappointing 1-1 draw, after Ben White's late goal was cancelled out by Federico Valverde's penalty in second-half stoppage time.

‌



Japan were up next and a much-changed England starting XI failed to break them down. Thomas Tuchel's side were beaten 1-0 thanks to a goal from Brighton's Kaoru Mitoma.

‌



However, despite these sub-par results, England have retained fourth place in FIFA's rankings. The same can't be said for a host of other teams and there is now a new No. 1.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Former Premier League star has wild World Cup nightclub celebration with arm in a sling READ MORE :

England supporters warned of ‘huge’ human rights risks at 2026 World Cup READ MORE :

Spain held the World No. 1 position heading into this international break. But after the Euro 2024 champions beat Serbia 3-0 last week, they were held to a 0-0 draw by Egypt.

‌



View 3 Images Spain were held by Egypt (Image: Getty)

This result has seen them drop to second in the rankings, with France taking over the top spot. Les Bleus beat Brazil 2-1 last month before a convincing 3-1 victory over Colombia.

Argentina round out the top four in third. This quartet will all be seeded at the upcoming World Cup and won't be able to meet each other until the semi-final stage. Portugal, Brazil and the Netherlands dwell just outside the top four, with the highest-ranked African nation in the rankings being Morocco in eighth.

‌



Italy remain in 12th place, despite their catastrophic playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina meaning they won't be competing in North America come the summer.

The hosts of the competition all rank within the top 30, with the United States at 16th, Mexico at 15th and Canada at 30th. The same cannot be said for other home nations.

View 3 Images Wales were defeated on penalties in Cardiff (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Wales were another team to suffer qualification heartbreak at the hands of Bosnia and they have dropped two places to 37th in the rankings. Scotland will be at the World Cup but their international break was poor enough to drop them five places to 43rd.

The Republic of Ireland were eliminated from World Cup contention by Czechia but remain at 59th in the FIFA rankings. Sports.title: Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged
Sports.content:
Premier League panel rule on controversial Man Utd penalty with official complaint lodged

Manchester United were left fuming that Amad was denied a penalty in their draw at Bournemouth, leading to an official complaint, but a Premier League panel has now backed the referee's decision

View 2 Images Man Utd were left fuming that they weren't awarded a penalty at Bournemouth

Manchester United have been told that both the referee and video assistant referee (VAR) were right to wave away Amad's controversial penalty appeal in their draw at Bournemouth last month.

‌



The Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has ruled on the decision, which left the United players and Michael Carrick stunned, and believes that the officials made the right call.

‌



Amad went down inside the area after Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert appeared to place two hands on him. Referee Stuart Attwell waved away the penalty appeals - with the visitor's anger only increasing when the Cherries went up the other end and scored through Ryan Christie in the 67th minute.

‌



United's frustration peaked as Matheus Cunha was given a penalty, which was then converted, for a challenge that looked extremely similar to the one Amad was on the receiving end of. The Red Devils made a formal complaint to the Premier League regarding the decision.

Since then the KMI Panel produced a split 3:2 vote against a spot-kick being awarded on the field. It was claimed that "whilst Truffert runs a risk, the contact made was not impactful and therefore below the high threshold for a foul". However two panellists said the action was "non-footballing" with a penalty the right call.

Harry Maguire charged by FA for reaction to Man Utd red card against Bournemouth READ MORE :

Matheus Cunha responds after Man Utd complaint and Harry Maguire fury READ MORE :

Despite those opinions the KMI Panel unanimously supported the VAR staying out of the situation, stating that it was "in keeping with the high threshold for VAR overturns".

‌



United would concede a late equaliser from the spot, which only added to Carrick's frustrations. He told Sky Sports: "We should have had another penalty. Obviously, if you get one, you must get the other. It's pretty much identical for me, two-hand grab. Either way, [the ref] got one wrong, but to give one and not give the other, I can't get my head around it. I think it's crazy. It's a bit baffling, really.

View 2 Images Amad saw his penalty appeals waved away (Image: Sky Sports)

"Because of that, they score and then it's chaos after that, really. We should have had another penalty and the game would have been totally different."

‌



Bruno Fernandes echoed that sentiment as he said: "We get a penalty against [us] where more or less it's the same situation as Amad. One is rewarded as a penalty, the other one not. I know it's difficult for the referee to give two penalties in the same game for the same team but what I don't understand is why VAR doesn't get involved in that situation.

"Either one is a penalty and the other one too or none of them is a penalty."

Sports.title: Haggerty ready for emotions of Bradford vs Leeds derby: 'We want to put on a show!'
Sports.content:
Bradford Bulls head coach Kurt Haggerty knows that this week has been a little bit different as his side prepare to face Leeds Rhinos in Super League for the first time in 12 years.

Go back to the early days of Super League and you are greeted with Bradford Bulls and Leeds Rhinos serving up some of Super League's best matches at the distinctive bowl of Odsal Stadium.

They were two titans of the early days, with 'Bullmania' taking charge before Leeds Rhinos took their crown.

As Leeds grew even bigger as the 'Golden Generation' of Danny McGuire, Rob Burrow, and Kevin Sinfield took control, Bradford's financial issues began to be laid bare until they were eventually relegated in 2014.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves

But now, 12 years on, Super League gets to see one of its most iconic derbies at the forefront once again. The first official Super League derby between Leeds and Bradford since 2014.

Intriguingly, there is just two points separating Leeds Rhinos in third and Bradford Bulls in sixth heading into this showdown.

How sweet it would be for Bradford to mark their return to the top flight with a derby win to remember on Good Friday on home turf.

They are looking to bounce back from their loss to Castleford while Leeds are flying high after they brought an end to Warrington's unbeaten start to the season.

For Bulls head coach Haggerty, it is not lost on him just how long the fans have waited for this moment and he hopes his side can keep in check of their emotions and "put on a show" at Odsal.

"You would be lying if you said this week didn't feel a little bit different," he said.

"This club has waited a long time for this game. The lads, you have felt the environment is palpable this week.

"It has hit a little bit different. We have probably had to manage the emotion around the game building up to it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Betfred Super League match between Castleford Tigers and Bradford Bulls

"We have had to pull back a bit and focus just on the game at the moment.

"Because one of these has not been played for such a long time, especially being a Super League game, there is a lot of emotion around both teams being Super League and the Bulls in particular being back in Super League.

"Playing a local derby, at Odsal, I don't think you get much bigger.

"Everybody had looked at the calendar to when Leeds at home was in particular.

"It is going to be a big day for the club, a huge day for the fans. I hope we can put a show on and give the best versions of ourselves in a local derby for our fans."
